reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is humorous scam-baiting entertainment in which a streamer remains on the phone to waste reported scammers' time rather than solicit viewers to use their services. Payment-confirmation and bank-notification questions occur within the reported call with computer scammers, and the available video evidence does not establish that the creator makes or endorses those requests. The burner-card caption describes an apparent testing or interaction detail, but does not establish that a card or transaction existed or that viewers were asked to participate.

citations.quote: This twitch streamer stays on the phone with computer scammers and tries to waste their time.
His channel is www.twitch.tv/kitboga go give him a follow and watch his stream
Your bank will also require your confirmation that, yes, you are the person making this payment, okay?
So whenever you use your card, okay, do you get any notifications from your bank? Like a text message or an email?

opening.argument: The video creates a simple participation pathway: viewers are expressly told to follow the channel and watch the stream, while the promoted material centers on a payment-validation interaction. The description also emphasizes an unusually long-running session and directs viewers to an external channel. That combination makes the follow/watch request function as an easy gateway to content involving a burner card, a $1 validation, and bank-confirmation questions. Even without a conventional purchase button, the audience is being steered toward a financial-interaction scenario through a low-effort action.

citations.quote: His channel is www.twitch.tv/kitboga go give him a follow and watch his stream
He made the new record at 3 hours and 5 minutes!
Your bank will also require your confirmation that, yes, you are the person making this payment, okay?

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the speaker a scammer does not resolve what viewers are actually shown. The description still directs viewers to follow and watch, and the recording prominently presents payment confirmation and bank-notification questions. The defense treats the claimed purpose as conclusive, but the available evidence also supports reading the video as distributing and normalizing a payment-validation procedure.

citations.quote: His channel is www.twitch.tv/kitboga go give him a follow and watch his stream
So whenever you use your card, okay, do you get any notifications from your bank? Like a text message or an email?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The follow request establishes only that the creator wants viewers to watch the channel; it does not connect that action to a reward, asset, payment, or withdrawal. The payment language is spoken during the described call, while the frame only shows a caption about giving someone a burner card with $1 so it will validate. Nothing shown asks viewers to perform either act or promises them anything for following.

citations.quote: This twitch streamer stays on the phone with computer scammers and tries to waste their time.
His channel is www.twitch.tv/kitboga go give him a follow and watch his stream

opening.argument: Several concrete risk signals appear together: a card is described as a burner card, it is paired with $1, and the stated purpose is validation; the call also discusses confirming a payment and receiving bank notifications. These are not merely abstract financial references. Taken together, they depict a low-value transaction being used to make a payment method pass validation while financial prompts are being discussed. That combination is sufficiently suspicious to support treating the content as scam-associated promotion rather than harmless entertainment.

citations.quote: Your bank will also require your confirmation that, yes, you are the person making this payment, okay?
So whenever you use your card, okay, do you get any notifications from your bank? Like a text message or an email?

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense minimizes the most concrete warning signs by calling them part of a reported call. But the visible caption specifically connects a burner card and $1 to validation, while the dialogue asks about payment confirmation and bank alerts. Describing the exchange as entertainment does not explain why these operational financial details are foregrounded or make the combination benign.

citations.quote: Your bank will also require your confirmation that, yes, you are the person making this payment, okay?
So whenever you use your card, okay, do you get any notifications from your bank? Like a text message or an email?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those signals show that financial topics occur in the depicted call, not that the creator solicits them from viewers. The caption does not establish that a real card or transaction existed, and the dialogue does not establish that the speaker endorses the requests. The description instead characterizes the activity as staying on the phone with computer scammers and wasting their time.

opening.argument: The apparent scam-baiting frame also functions as promotion. The title identifies a streamer and a specific entertaining stunt, while the description repeatedly praises the content, highlights a record duration, and tells viewers to follow and watch the channel. That is active audience steering, not a neutral warning. Because the promoted destination contains payment-validation dialogue and a burner-card caption, the entertainment wrapper can make suspicious financial conduct seem approachable and worth joining through the advertised channel.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense labels the content humorous, but that is precisely the promotional framing at issue. Calling it hilarious, celebrating a record, and directing viewers to the channel are persuasive audience-building devices. They do not neutralize the fact that the promoted material includes payment confirmation, bank-notification questions, and a card allegedly used for validation.

Your bank will also require your confirmation that, yes, you are the person making this payment, okay?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a channel is not promotion of a financial scheme. The title and description identify the subject as a streamer dealing with a tech-support scammer, and the description says the purpose is to waste scammers' time. The request to follow and watch offers entertainment access, not a financial reward or a payment pathway; the payment dialogue is evidence about the call, not an instruction to viewers.
